draft.text:
**Following a Request Through Datasette: The App, Its Views, Plugins and Permissions**

The plan follows one request: the app is built, plugins register themselves, permissions get defined, and then a request is routed to a view and answered. It runs to about 17 sittings, and I left out templates, facets, publishing and the command line to keep to the request path. I could only see the opening lines of four files, so each section points at whole files and not specific lines.

ops.text: 1. The App Object at the Centre
ops.description: What the single app object is, what it holds and why everything else reaches back to it.

ops.text: What the app is made of
ops.description: The imports at the top show the pieces the app pulls together: async work, templates, signing, threads. [files: datasette/app.py]
How the app is created and what it keeps for the life of the server. [files: datasette/app.py]

ops.text: Why views and plugins are handed the app
ops.description: The app is passed around as the one shared handle. [files: datasette/app.py, datasette/hookspecs.py]

ops.text: 2. Plugins and the Points They Plug Into
ops.description: How extension points are declared and how plugins attach to them.
Each hook is a named function with a signature and a one-line purpose, from startup to page styling. [files: datasette/hookspecs.py]

ops.text: The plugin manager and the built-in plugins
ops.description: The manager is created, the hook list is registered, and the default plugin list is loaded. [files: datasette/plugins.py]
Where the app asks the manager for every plugin's answer and uses the results. [files: datasette/app.py, datasette/plugins.py]
The permission model that views will consult before answering.
What is being asked about (an action) and what it is asked of (a database, table or row). [files: datasette/permissions.py, datasette/resources.py, datasette/default_actions.py]

The default permission plugins contribute allow and deny rules through hooks. [files: datasette/default_permissions/__init__.py, datasette/default_permissions/defaults.py, datasette/default_permissions/config.py]

ops.text: Who is asking: actors, tokens and cookies
ops.description: How a request is tied to an actor. [files: datasette/actor_auth_cookie.py, datasette/tokens.py, datasette/default_permissions/tokens.py]
The path from the incoming request to the right view.
The wrappers every view receives and returns. [files: datasette/utils/asgi.py]

ops.text: Matching a path to a view
ops.description: The app's route table and how it picks a view. [files: datasette/app.py, datasette/utils/asgi.py]
Where plugins can wrap the app, and where cross-site protection sits. [files: datasette/app.py, datasette/csrf.py, datasette/hookspecs.py]
What a view does between receiving a request and returning a response.
The common behaviour views inherit, including the error type they raise. [files: datasette/views/base.py]
How a view asks the app whether the actor is allowed. [files: datasette/views/base.py, datasette/views/index.py, datasette/app.py]

ops.text: Home, database, table and row pages
ops.description: How each view fetches data and chooses its output format. [files: datasette/views/index.py, datasette/views/database.py, datasette/views/table.py, datasette/views/row.py]
How failures and refusals travel back out to the visitor.
How a raised error becomes an error page or JSON. [files: datasette/views/base.py, datasette/handle_exception.py]
What happens on a denied request, and how a plugin can change it. [files: datasette/forbidden.py, datasette/hookspecs.py]
